Chapter Two: Lost and Alone in a Vast, Unfamiliar City
Picture this: it’s evening, and the boy’s older brother comes up with an idea—why not try to earn a little extra money at the train station? For them, that place is almost like a second home. The thought of helping out and maybe even treating themselves feels like a real adventure. So, off they go, weaving through the bustling crowds and all that noise, sticking close together because, honestly, there’s nothing quite like the bond between brothers.
As the night stretches on, exhaustion starts to set in. The younger brother can barely keep his eyes open and finally begs for a break. His brother reassures him, promising to come back soon, and tells him to wait on a bench. The boy settles in, trusting his brother’s word, and drifts off into a deep sleep—comforted by the belief that he’ll wake up to a familiar face.
But when he does wake up, everything’s changed. The station is quiet now, almost eerie. The crowds have vanished, and his brother is nowhere to be seen. Can you imagine that kind of panic? Still, he clings to what he was told: just wait. Hours creep by. The station feels emptier and colder, and fear starts to gnaw at him. Eventually, hunger and confusion push him to board a stationary train nearby—hoping, maybe, that it’ll lead him back to his brother or at least home.
But that train isn’t what he expects. Suddenly, it lurches forward, carrying him away from everything he knows. Out the window, familiar fields melt into a never-ending cityscape. By the time the train stops, he steps out into the chaos of Kolkata—a city that feels like another world. The faces are unfamiliar, the language is strange, and he’s completely alone.
Wandering the city streets, he’s overwhelmed by everything: the endless noise, the crush of people, the constant movement. He’s hungry and scared, and quickly learns to be careful around strangers. Sometimes, someone offers a bit of food or a place to rest, but he also runs into people who are anything but kind. Staying safe becomes a daily challenge.
Every night, he finds a doorway to sleep in. He scavenges for scraps, relying on pure instinct to survive. All the while, memories of home—his mother’s gentle face, his brother’s laughter—come and go. They comfort him, but they also hurt, reminding him just how much he’s lost. Still, every day, he hopes he’ll find a way back. But the city is huge, and it’s easy to feel swallowed up by it all.
Most of us never really know what it’s like to be that lost—to lose not just your place, but your sense of safety, your language, even who you are. For this child, every day is a new test: can he make it through, can he find a little hope to hold onto?
But you know, even in the darkest moments, kindness finds a way to shine through. Maybe it’s a warm meal from a stranger. Maybe it’s a group of children sharing a place to sleep, or someone pointing the way to a shelter. These small acts become lifelines—little reminders that hope isn’t gone, even when everything else seems out of reach.
Days slip into weeks. The details of home start to blur, but the longing never fades. That deep, unbreakable hope of finding his family again, of belonging somewhere, keeps him going. And it’s that hope—the courage to keep searching, even when the way forward is uncertain—that truly defines his journey.
